item.title: Fractional Fefferman--Stein inequalities on infinite rooted $k$-ary trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.08653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study weighted endpoint estimates for the centered fractional maximal operator on the infinite rooted $k$-ary tree, $T$. Our first result is a Fefferman--Stein type estimate \[ w\bigl(\{M_\alpha f>\lambda\}\bigr) \lesssim_{\alpha,s} \frac1\lambda\sum_{x\in T}|f(x)|M_{\alpha,s}w(x), \qquad s>1, \] with a constant independent of the branching parameter $k$. Although the proof is inspired by the non-fractional argument of Ombrosi, Rivera-R\'ios and Safe in \cite{ORRS}, the fractional normalization introduces a genuinely new scale interaction. At radius $r$, one must renormalize the function by $k^{r\alpha}$ while keeping the dyadic cutoff at $k^r$; this leads to a new summation mechanism involving simultaneously $k^{r\alpha}$ and $k^{r(1-\alpha)}$. We then study sharpness and the geometry of admissible weights. We construct counterexamples showing that the estimate cannot in general be reduced to $s=1$ for any $0<\alpha<1$. In the subcritical range $0<\alpha<1/2$, we characterize power-type radial weights satisfying the natural fractional $A_1$ condition and prove that the failure persists after any fixed finite number of iterations of $M_\alpha$. We also prove that $M_\alpha w\lesssim w$ is necessary for the corresponding weighted weak type estimate but is not sufficient in the subcritical range. Finally, we identify a phase transition: for $1/2\le\alpha<1$ no nonzero global weight can satisfy $M_\alpha w\lesssim w$.
item.dc:creator: Gonzalo Iba\~nez-Firnkorn, Jorgelina Recchi

item.title: Walsh Analysis in the Twenty-First Century: Convergence, Summability, Nonlinear Approximation, Universality, and Digital Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.09010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Walsh analysis connects ordered Fourier convergence, summability, nonlinear approximation, and universal representation through a common character algebra. This survey examines developments from 2000-2026 against their classical foundations. Binary kernel geometry explains Hardy-space losses and summability thresholds; interval and packet methods control spectral selection; localized blocks produce correction and universal representations with distinct coefficient and exceptional-set requirements. Selected proofs and counterexamples compare these mechanisms and identify where an implication needs an additional hypothesis. The same distinctions organize digital integration, sparse measurements, Boolean spectra, and generalized Walsh bases. Quantitative thresholds, source conventions, and published theorem pointers are collected in comparative tables. The concluding problems separate source-listed questions, proposed refinements, and elementary obstructions. Supplementary derivations preserve normalization checks and finite covariance calculations while keeping the main exposition focused on the analytic mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: Sergo A. Episkoposian

item.title: A sharp weighted $L^2$ Bernstein inequality for partial derivatives on the unit ball
item.description: arXiv:2611.09306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the sharp constant in the weighted $L^2$ Bernstein inequality for coordinate derivatives on the unit ball with a Jacobi weight and the strengthened derivative factors introduced by Beberok and Xu. The constant is expressed in terms of the largest zeros of Jacobi polynomials, and all extremal polynomials are characterized explicitly. The proof uses an orthogonal polynomial decomposition that gives diagonal formulas for both the squared norm and the weighted derivative integral. We also obtain two-sided bounds for the sharp constant and determine its leading asymptotic behavior as the polynomial degree tends to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Beberok

item.title: Liouville transforms for ordinary differential equations with distributional coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.08661v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Liouville transforms for the differential equation $Ju'+qu=wf$ on the real interval $(a,b)$ where $J$ is a constant, invertible, skew-hermitian matrix and $q$ and $w$ are matrices whose entries are distributions of order $0$ with $q$ Hermitian and $w$ non-negative. In particular, we examine their use in the treatment of quasi-regular endpoints and their impact on the Weyl-Titchmarsh $\mathbb M$-function associated with the differential equation.
item.dc:creator: Rudi Weikard

item.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.09887v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$, for a bounded connected open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$. Consequently, every coercive, weakly lower semicontinuous energy on this space attains its minimum over $\mathcal{N}_N$. This covers the Deep Ritz method with convex integrands, Sobolev training and Lipschitz learning. Moreover, as the weight decay parameter tends to zero, minimizers of the regularized problem converge, up to subsequences, to minimizers with minimal parameter norm. We also prove that the set of ReLU networks with two hidden layers of bounded widths is not closed in $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ or in $C(\overline\Omega)$. This disproves a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan and Voigtlaender.
item.dc:creator: Eloi Martinet, Leon Bungert

item.title: Periodic solutions of symmetric Hamiltonian systems
item.description: arXiv:1906.02463v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of periodic solutions of Hamiltonian system $\dot z(t)=J \nabla H(z(t))$, where $H$ is symmetric under an action of a compact Lie group. We are looking for periodic solutions in a nearby of non-isolated critical points of $H$ which form orbits of the group action. We prove Lyapunov-type theorem for symmetric Hamiltonian systems.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Strzelecki

item.title: Factorized $q$-difference equations and their fundamental solutions
item.description: arXiv:2305.12754v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct fundamental solutions of a class of factorized $q$-difference equations in terms of Jacobi theta functions and Zwegers' $\mu$-functions. To obtain a formal series solution $f_0$ for a factorized $q$-difference equation, we present a $q$-analogue of the fundamental relation (often called the Wronski-type relation) between the elementary symmetric polynomials and the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials. We also provide some formulas for the image of the $q$-Borel summation of the formal series solution $f_0$. As an application, we give another proof of the expressions due to S. Y. Kang and S. P. Zwegers of the universal mock theta functions and higher level Appell functions in terms of $\mu$-functions.
item.dc:creator: Satoshi Tsuchimi

item.title: Multilinear extrapolation on Banach function spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.35364v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We solve an open problem on the multilinear Rubio de Francia extrapolation on Banach function spaces. The main result states that, under the assumption of the boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, the multivariable boundedness on Banach function spaces can be extrapolated from some weighted Lebesgue space, including the cases where some exponents may be infinite. Based on this result, we also establish multilinear extrapolation of boundedness on rearrangement invariant Banach function spaces, and multilinear extrapolation of compactness on general Banach function spaces. Beyond that, we give characterizations of the boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on both general Banach function spaces and certain specific function spaces. All results do not require any convexity or concavity conditions on Banach function spaces. The main ingredients in the proof are a multilinear version of the Rubio de Francia algorithm, a stopping-time argument, convex analysis, and a compactness criterion on Banach function spaces. As applications of extrapolation theorems, we obtain multilinear extrapolation for the boundedness and compactness of commutators on Banach function spaces. These results can be further applied to specific operators, which cover both the full range case including multilinear Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund operators, multilinear pseudo-differential operators, and bilinear paraproducts, and the limited range case including the bilinear Hilbert transform, multilinear rough singular integrals, and bilinear oscillatory Fourier multipliers.
item.dc:creator: Mingming Cao

item.title: Another Application of the Alternating Map: Time-and-Band Limiting
item.description: arXiv:2611.01839v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Castillo's dual equations for the alternating map reduce polynomial time-and-band limiting to two scalar problems. We determine the concentration multiplicities at a single cutoff, with sharp finite support and moment requirements. When the scalar problems admit irreducible tridiagonal commutants, we classify every real symmetric pentadiagonal commutant of the simple concentration matrix and construct one with simple spectrum. Its half-bandwidth is minimal for $N\ge3$ in polynomial degree order. Laguerre, Jacobi and Meixner input give applications; the constructions of Castro and Gr\"unbaum follow by specialization. We give spectral-gap and rounding bounds, and certify small concentration values and deficits for noninteger Jacobi parameters.
item.dc:creator: L. Tertuliano da Silva

item.title: A Novel Two-Parameter Penalty: Relaxation Degree Analysis and Sparse Signal Recovery
item.description: arXiv:2603.09722v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we introduce a nonconvex two-parameter penalty function $P_{a,p}$, parameterized by $a\in(0,\infty)$ and $p\in(0,1]$, and the relaxation degree RD$_P$ for a separable nonconvex penalty function $P$. Based on $P_{a,p}$, we further propose the $P_{a,p}$ minimization framework for sparse signal recovery. This framework generalizes the TL1 minimization model established by S. Zhang and J. Xin (corresponding to the special case $p=1$) and provides a unified family of nonconvex penalty functions for sparse signal recovery. Using the sparse convex-combination technique, we establish both exact and stable sparse signal recovery under the restricted isometry property (RIP). To efficiently solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, we apply a modified iteratively re-weighted least squares method and the difference of convex functions algorithm (DCA) to develop the IRLSTLp algorithm for unconstrained $P_{a,p}$ minimization and prove some convergence results. Finally, numerical experiments compare recovery and runtime against single- and double-loop baselines, examine sensitivity to $(a,p)$, and assess the empirical correlation between RD$_{P_{a,p}}$ and recovery within the proposed family.
item.dc:creator: Ziwei Li, Wengu Chen, Huanmin Ge, Dachun Yang

item.title: Multiplicity-Weighted Moments of a Two-Monomial Harmonic Map Beyond the Caustic
item.description: arXiv:2609.28370v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While the Jacobian of a planar harmonic mapping keeps a constant sign, the signed and the unsigned area elements agree up to that sign, and the two natural moment hierarchies coincide. Once the Jacobian changes sign the critical circle acquires a caustic as its image, part of the plane is covered several times with opposite orientations, and the hierarchies part company: integrating a radial weight against $J_F$ lets overlapping sheets cancel, giving the degree-weighted moments $J_n$, while integrating against $|J_F|$ lets every sheet count positively, giving the multiplicity-weighted moments $J_n^{\pm}$. These are the classical degree and area formulas for the same map, the second weighted by the multiplicity function (Banach indicatrix). It is the second family, the one the caustic threatens, for which a closed form is no longer automatic. For the two-monomial map $F(w)=w+iC\bar w^{k}$ on an annulus we show that it has one anyway: $J_n^{\pm}$ is the total variation of the very same explicit primitive whose endpoint difference gives $J_n$. Crossing the caustic therefore costs exactly one extra evaluation point, the critical radius $r_*=(k|C|)^{-1/(k-1)}$, and it is the same point for every order $n$: the weight $|F|^{2n}$ is nonnegative and so contributes no sign change of its own. On the degree-weighted side $J_n$ has a boundary-only closed form for every $n\ge0$, the zeroth being the signed area of the image counted with degree, and the complex-weighted moments vanish unless $(k+1)\mid(m-\ell)$. Neither weighted integral is a new object, and the caustic of this family has been located before in the literature on harmonic trinomials; what is new is the closed evaluation of the multiplicity-weighted hierarchy across it.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as B\'odis
